market_summary: Pre-market, Thursday 26 November 2026 (as of 08:33 IST). In the previous cash session on Wednesday 25 November, the Nifty 50 rose 1.85% to 25,819.25 and the Sensex gained 1.82% to 83,938.28. Reuters reported gains in 14 of 16 major sectors; financials rose 2.2% and IT 1.1%, while mid-caps added 0.3% and small-caps fell 0.4%, pointing to a large-cap-led rebound rather than uniformly strong breadth. GIFT Nifty was 26,061.5 at 08:01 IST, indicating a firmer opening bias, with 26,000 identified by Reuters as an important near-term resistance area. Asian equities recovered modestly overnight, but AI/technology volatility and the proposed US tariff framework remain risks. Brent rose about 3.5% to $94.90/bbl, and traders expected USD/INR to open at 92.32–92.36 versus Wednesday's 92.23 close. Provisional 25 November cash flows showed FPI/FII net buying of ₹4,479.08 crore and DII net buying of ₹4,018.72 crore. US Q3 GDP was revised to 4.3% annualised; October core PCE inflation was 3.3% year on year. Portfolio check: the latest accessible holdings snapshot is dated 12 November 2026 and is not live; HDFC Bank is a recorded name and its 25 November director re-appointment filing is highlighted below. Facts are distinguished from interpretation in each item; no guaranteed calls or financial advice.

global_cues.title: GIFT Nifty indicates a firmer opening; 26,000 is a key test
global_cues.detail: Reuters recorded GIFT Nifty futures at 26,061.5 at 08:01 IST on 26 November, versus the Nifty 50 cash close of 25,819.25 on 25 November. Reuters cited 26,000 as a key resistance area. This is a futures indication, not a live cash-index price or a guaranteed opening level.

global_cues.title: Asian markets rebound, but risk appetite remains fragile
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported Japan's Nikkei up 1.6%, South Korea's main index up 1.9%, and Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan up 0.6% early Thursday after Wall Street recovered from steep intraday losses. Nvidia remained under pressure after S&P put its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade. Interpretation: the regional bounce is constructive for sentiment, but does not remove technology and AI-investment volatility.

global_cues.title: Proposed US tariffs leave India facing a trade-negotiation risk
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported that the US administration proposed levies on imports from 14 trading partners. The US Trade Representative said the tariff on Indian imports would be capped at 17% if a trade deal is reached, or rise to 25% if talks fail. These are conditional policy outcomes, not a confirmed final tariff schedule.

global_cues.title: US cash equity markets are closed for Thanksgiving
global_cues.detail: Nasdaq's official 2026 calendar lists 26 November as a full market closure and 27 November as an early close at 1:00 p.m. ET. The holiday removes the normal US cash-equity session as a fresh overnight signal for Indian markets.

global_cues.title: US growth data were strong while core inflation remained elevated
global_cues.detail: The US Bureau of Economic Analysis revised Q3 2026 real GDP growth to 4.3% annualised from the 3.4% advance estimate. Its October Personal Income and Outlays release showed core PCE prices up 0.3% month on month and 3.3% year on year. Interpretation: stronger growth is supportive for demand, while sticky core inflation can constrain the Federal Reserve's policy flexibility.
global_cues.source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, releases dated 25 Nov 2026

intraday.headline: NSE filing discloses BP finance-operations partnership involving about 3,000 employee transfers
intraday.what_changed: Verified fact: Wipro's Regulation 30 press release filed with NSE and BSE says BP selected Wipro as a strategic supplier to transform BP's core finance operations. Around 3,000 BP employees supporting finance operations in India, Hungary and Malaysia are expected to move to Wipro. The new operating model is expected to take effect in 2027, subject to applicable conditions. The filing does not disclose contract value or tenure; BP retains accountability for standards, controls, data and technology governance, with PwC providing controls oversight.
intraday.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the arrangement could add scale to Wipro's finance and business-process services and create scope for AI- and automation-led transformation work. Without disclosed contract economics, the revenue, margin and earnings contribution cannot yet be quantified.
intraday.risk: No contract value, duration, country-wise employee split or detailed transition costs were disclosed. The operating model is conditional and starts in 2027; employee transfer and integration may affect near-term costs before benefits are realised.
intraday.source: Wipro Limited, Regulation 30 press release filed with NSE/BSE, 25 Nov 2026, 15:48 IST

swing.headline: FY2026 Q4 results show 81.5% PAT growth; board recommends ₹12 per-share dividend
swing.what_changed: Verified fact from the company's 25 November release: Q4 FY2026 new orders rose 92.1% year on year to ₹4,514 crore and order backlog increased 25.6% to ₹20,362 crore. Revenue from operations rose 30.4% to ₹3,453 crore; profit after tax rose 81.5% to ₹653 crore; EBIT margin improved to 22.6% from 16.9%. FY2026 revenue was ₹10,243 crore, up 30.9%. The board recommended a dividend of ₹12 per equity share of face value ₹2, subject to the applicable approval process.
swing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: strong order intake, a larger backlog and improved operating margin support near-term execution visibility and demonstrate operating leverage. The dividend recommendation adds a shareholder-return event, but it is not yet a completed payment.
swing.risk: Backlog conversion, project execution, capacity expansion and working-capital needs remain key risks. The company also disclosed a ₹2,060 crore transformer-capacity investment plan; actual returns depend on timely execution and demand. Dividend remains subject to approval.
swing.source: Siemens Energy India Limited, official Q4 FY2026 press release, 25 Nov 2026 (NSE filing time reported as 20:19 IST)

investing.headline: Board approves five-year re-appointment of Harsh Kumar Bhanwala as independent director
investing.what_changed: Verified fact: HDFC Bank's Regulation 30 filing to NSE and BSE states that the board approved the re-appointment of Dr. Harsh Kumar Bhanwala as an independent director for five years, from 25 January 2027 through 24 January 2032, subject to shareholder approval. The filing notes that he is not related to other directors or key managerial personnel and is not debarred from holding office.
investing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: this is a governance-continuity update relevant to a tracked portfolio name, rather than a direct change to earnings, capital or asset quality. Bhanwala's disclosed experience includes leadership at NABARD and IIFCL.
investing.risk: Shareholder approval remains pending. The appointment announcement by itself does not establish a change in operating performance, credit quality or valuation.
investing.source: HDFC Bank Limited, Regulation 30 filing to NSE/BSE, 25 Nov 2026, 18:01 IST

macro.name: FPI/FII and DII cash-market flows
macro.value: FPI/FII net +₹4,479.08 crore; DII net +₹4,018.72 crore
macro.context: Provisional cash-market flows for Wednesday 25 November 2026. Both investor groups were net buyers; figures are provisional and may be revised. Reuters independently reported FPI net buying of ₹44.79 billion.

macro.name: Brent crude
macro.value: About US$94.90 per barrel; up approximately 3.5%
macro.context: Reuters reported the overnight rise amid concerns about Middle East supply disruption following Houthi claims of an attack on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery. Higher crude is a headwind for India's import bill and fuel-sensitive sectors; the quote is an overnight reported level, not a live tick.

macro.name: USD/INR
macro.value: Expected open ₹92.32–₹92.36 per US dollar; Wednesday close ₹92.23
macro.context: Trader indications cited by Reuters point to a slightly weaker rupee open after Brent rose. This is an expected opening range, not a confirmed spot quote.

macro.name: US Q3 2026 real GDP, second estimate
macro.value: +4.3% annualised, revised from the +3.4% advance estimate
macro.context: The BEA said growth accelerated from +2.2% in Q2 2026. The second estimate reflected upward revisions primarily to investment and consumer spending.
macro.source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, 25 Nov 2026

macro.name: US October 2026 core PCE price index
macro.value: +0.3% month on month; +3.3% year on year
macro.context: The BEA reported the same 0.3% monthly rise for headline PCE prices, while headline PCE inflation was 3.8% year on year. Core inflation remains relevant to Federal Reserve rate expectations.
macro.source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, Personal Income and Outlays, 25 Nov 2026
